title: Lower the ceiling

predict.q: The ceiling is $15. It is cut to $10. What happens to the shortage?

options.s: It shrinks, because goods are now cheaper
options.fb: Cheaper means more is supplied? No: a lower price makes firms supply less, so the gap grows.

options.s: It grows, because more is demanded and less is supplied
options.fb: Qd rises 70 → 80 and Qs falls 40 → 20: the shortage doubles from 30 to 60.

options.s: It stays the same, because only the price changes
options.fb: The price change moves both quantities: buyers want more, sellers offer less.

task: Move the ceiling slider and watch Qd, Qs and the shortage. Then try the supply-elasticity settings: a flatter supply curve makes the shortage bigger at the same ceiling.

target.do: Cut the ceiling from $15 to $10, then press Check.

takeaway: The lower the ceiling, and the more elastic demand and supply are, the bigger the shortage.
